items.action: Update LXD/MicroCloud snaps and verify the installed version after refresh, as fixed releases were still rolling out; restrict who can reach the LXD API in the meantime.
items.details: Fixed in LXD 6.10.1, 5.21.9, 5.0.11 and 4.0.15, and MicroCloud 3.4.1 and 2.1.5; Incus, which reported the flaw, fixed it in 7.6.0. No known exploitation, no CISA KEV listing and no working exploit published as of October 30. There is no configuration workaround beyond restricting network access to the API.
items.summary: Canonical fixed CVE-2026-112816, a certificate-validation flaw in LXD and MicroCloud that lets an attacker with network access to the HTTPS API authenticate as any trusted TLS client using only that client's public certificate.
items.title: CVSS 10.0 LXD flaw lets attackers impersonate trusted clients without a private key

items.action: Confirm Cisco, GitLab and Ivanti fixes are applied — not just scheduled — and check GitLab and Ivanti instances for signs of the reported exploitation.
items.details: Cisco's flaw lets an unauthenticated remote attacker force a firewall reload via the Remote Access SSL VPN when secondary authentication is configured in the tunnel group; GitLab's is an integer overflow in the CI/CD regex compiler allowing unauthenticated code execution. Alpine Linux reported attempted exploitation of its GitLab server on October 20-21 and rebuilt it, unable to rule out code execution. No new KEV entries were added on October 31 or November 1; the catalog stood at version 2026.10.30 with 1,766 entries.
items.summary: CISA's remediation deadlines for actively exploited Cisco ASA/FTD flaw CVE-2026-76418 (CVSS 8.6) and GitLab flaw CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS 10.0) fell on November 1, with Ivanti Connect Secure CVE-2026-111357 due November 2.
items.title: KEV deadlines land: Cisco and GitLab due Nov 1, Ivanti due today

items.action: Update to WordPress 7.1.4 and check logs for suspicious requests to PHP files under wp-content/upgrade, plus unfamiliar admin accounts, plugins or PHP files.
items.details: The flaw affects WordPress Core 4.7 through 7.1.3, carries a CVSS score of 8.1, and has no CVE identifier in the reviewed disclosures. Attackers poll predictable staging paths under wp-content/upgrade, trying to catch the brief window while a full-package update unpacks. Blocked attempts are not confirmed compromises.
items.summary: Wordfence blocked 62,969 attacks in 24 hours targeting a WordPress Core remote code execution flaw in the core-update process, patched in WordPress 7.1.4 on October 28.
items.title: WordPress RCE flaw draws nearly 63,000 attack attempts in 24 hours

items.action: Crypto and financial service providers should check blocklists against the FBI alert's addresses, including funds derived from them, and watch for ETH conversions through DeFi and instant-swap services.
items.details: The FBI, with the US Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation, said it observed TraderTraitor actors converting stolen assets primarily into Ethereum and expected further laundering via DeFi and instant-swap services. It published wallet addresses tied to the theft and asked service providers to block transactions involving them. TRM Labs put the movement at about $6.36 billion across ten blockchains in roughly 20 minutes, the largest crypto theft on record.
items.summary: The FBI said North Korea was responsible for stealing more than $6 billion in virtual assets from Binance on or about October 29, naming the TraderTraitor group, also tracked as Lazarus Group and APT38.
items.title: FBI attributes $6bn+ Binance theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor

items.action: Treat the listing as a claim pending confirmation; healthcare-sector defenders should watch for Qilin double-extortion tactics and review exposed credentials and public-facing applications.
items.details: The listing date reflects when the victim appeared on the leak site and may differ from the date of initial compromise. The specific data taken and the extent of any encryption have not been independently verified in the reviewed reporting.
items.summary: Qilin listed fzmb GmbH (Forschungszentrum für Medizintechnik und Biotechnologie), a German healthcare-sector organisation, on its leak site on November 1, 2026.
items.title: Qilin lists German healthcare research firm fzmb GmbH on leak site

items.action: Treat as an unverified claim; organisations with similar exposure should rotate exposed credentials, enforce MFA and hunt for infostealer compromise.
items.details: The claim was tracked via the Ransomware.live platform. Tracker reporting linked the incident to infostealer activity and cited 103 exposed passwords, 27 of them classified as critical. The scope of any encryption or data theft has not been confirmed by the victim in the reviewed reporting.
items.summary: LockBit5 published PT Synergy Risk Management Consultants (synergy.co.id) as a victim on its leak site on November 1, 2026, according to ransomware trackers.
items.title: LockBit5 claims Indonesian consultancy PT Synergy Risk Management

items.action: AU Small Finance Bank auto-loan customers should watch for phishing using loan/KYC details; banks should review third-party SaaS data holdings and cyber-insurance notification duties.
items.details: The bank holds a ₹100 crore cyber insurance cover from New India Assurance but had not yet intimated the insurer, according to people familiar with the matter cited on November 2. The extent of potential exposure and the number of customers affected are yet to be established. The bank has said its own systems remain unaffected. The reporting notes this follows cyberattacks involving Bank of Baroda and State Bank of India.
items.summary: AU Small Finance Bank is investigating a potential data breach involving a third-party Salesforce-hosted platform holding information related to auto loan customers, and insurers are watching rising cyber claims across Indian banks.
items.title: AU Small Finance Bank leak probe raises insurer concerns; extent still unestablished

items.action: Do not treat the 30GB figure as proof of a breach; verify provenance and samples before acting, and watch for supplier-impersonation and invoice-fraud attempts using any genuine records if confirmed.
items.details: The claim was flagged on November 2 by Dark Web Intelligence (@DailyDarkWeb). No detailed description of the allegedly stolen information, sample records or screenshots were provided in the reported post. The incident should be treated as an unverified threat-actor claim, not confirmation of a breach; the dataset could be genuine, recycled, or incorrectly attributed.
items.summary: A threat actor allegedly published an approximately 30GB dataset attributed to Parle Agro, maker of Frooti and Appy Fizz, as a free download on a dark web forum — with no samples, file listing or company statement to establish authenticity.
items.title: Parle Agro 30GB dark-web data leak claim is unverified

items.action: Prioritise configuration and credential hygiene, least-privilege access and third-party vendor monitoring over assuming only advanced attackers are the risk.
items.details: The analysis examined incidents involving ICMR, CoWIN, State Bank of India, AIIMS Delhi and data-selling networks uncovered by police. It also found breaches are often detected first by private firms or researchers rather than the affected organisations, and flagged pirated or unauthorised software as an added risk. The findings point to regular audits, stronger authentication, restricted privileges and continuous monitoring.
items.summary: A recent central-agency analysis of major Indian data-leak incidents found recurring failures — misconfigured servers, compromised credentials, insider involvement, weak access controls and inadequate third-party monitoring — rather than only sophisticated attacks.
items.title: Government analysis flags basic lapses behind India's major data leaks
